stem: A rock-salt $MX$ crystal has $1.0\times10^{22}$ unit cells, each with $4$ formula units. Its molar mass is $100\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. If it loses $0.020\ \text{g}$ solely through Schottky defects, what percentage of its cation sites are vacant? Take $N_A=6.0\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Schottky defects remove one MX formula unit per vacancy pair. Formula units lost = (0.020/100)×6.0×10²³ = 1.2×10²⁰. Cation sites = 1.0×10²²×4 = 4.0×10²². Vacancy percentage = (1.2×10²⁰/4.0×10²²)×100 = 0.30%.

working:
Moles of Schottky pairs formed $=\dfrac{0.020}{100}=2.0	imes10^{-4}\ 	ext{mol}$.
Number of cation vacancies $=2.0	imes10^{-4}	imes6.0	imes10^{23}=1.2	imes10^{20}$.
Total cation sites $=4	imes1.0	imes10^{22}=4.0	imes10^{22}$.
Vacant percentage $=\dfrac{1.2	imes10^{20}}{4.0	imes10^{22}}	imes100=0.30\%$.

Independent check: Schottky defects remove one MX formula unit per vacancy pair. Formula units lost = (0.020/100)×6.0×10²³ = 1.2×10²⁰. Cation sites = 1.0×10²²×4 = 4.0×10²². Vacancy percentage = (1.2×10²⁰/4.0×10²²)×100 = 0.30%.
solution:
Each Schottky pair removes one $MX$ formula unit, so the number of cation vacancies is
$$\frac{0.020}{100}\times 6.0\times10^{23}=1.2\times10^{20}.$$
Total cation sites $=4\times1.0\times10^{22}=4.0\times10^{22}$; hence vacancy percentage $=\dfrac{1.2\times10^{20}}{4.0\times10^{22}}\times100=0.30\%$.
